answer: Running a farm as a result means funding each extra identity through a waiting period with no reward, which is a capital cost an honest single agent burns once and never again. Because the age is read from the inlet checkpoint rather than self-declared, the harbor audit can recompute it and a backdated claim fails. An identity must be at least 7 epochs old on the cipher ledger before its answer counts toward quorum, which makes fresh keys useless at the moment they are cheapest to mint. That is 9 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
